title: Anger and Frustration
summary: Quick temper, how anger builds in the body, what follows, and the calming skills a person already has.
clinicianNotes: Ask about any risk of harm to self or others and follow your own protocol. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

guidance.ok: On quick temper, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On quick temper, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask what has changed recently and what is behind the short fuse.
guidance.explore: On quick temper, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask what has changed recently and what is behind the short fuse.

domains.label: Body and build-up
domains.description: Physical signs and long build-up of anger.

guidance.ok: On body and build-up, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On body and build-up, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore early body signals and the thoughts that feed the build-up.
guidance.explore: On body and build-up, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore early body signals and the thoughts that feed the build-up.

domains.label: Aftermath
domains.description: Regret and the effect on relationships and work.

guidance.ok: On aftermath, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On aftermath, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore the costs and what the person wishes they had done instead.
guidance.explore: On aftermath, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore the costs and what the person wishes they had done instead.

domains.label: Calming skills
domains.description: Cooling down and saying what is needed.

guidance.ok: On calming skills, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On calming skills, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on the skills already in use and plan one new one.
guidance.explore: On calming skills, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on the skills already in use and plan one new one.

items.text: I lose my temper faster than I used to.
People say I am easily annoyed.
My heart pounds or my jaw tightens when I get angry.
Anger builds up for hours before I let it out.
I replay what made me angry long after it happened.
I regret things I said or did when angry.
My anger has caused trouble in my relationships.
My anger has caused problems at work or in public.
I can step away and cool down before I respond.
I know what usually sets my anger off.
I can say what I need without shouting.
